newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares lose 2.74 percent on profit taking.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares lose 2.74 percent on profit taking.

text.p: Istanbul shares retreated from a high of 2,018 in early morning to end the day at 1,955, 2.74 percent or 55 points lower than Friday's close.
Stocks fell on profit taking and awaited technical correction while state enterprise stocks led the fall with giant flat steel producer Eregli easing 1,000 lira to 24,500.
Daily volume slipped to 20.57 trillion lira ($132.6 million), compared to Friday's 25.83 trillion lira ($167 million).
"State owned enterprises and stocks with large market capitalisations which had the most impact on index calculations were sold selectively" said Kursat Oral from Meksa Securities.
"I expect the index to give a reaction from a 1,950 level of support tomorrow, but I expect trade volume to remain in a tight range," he said.

"The mid-year profit forecests of private sector companies as well as political developments this week should direct investments from state shares to private sector stocks," Gokhan Kolay from Polen Securities said.
